answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making reputation non-transferable and earned only from attested, useful work over time, like tending a garden rather than planting flags overnight. A newcomer gets a narrow quota: few trades, small stakes, and every job checked by established peers. As verified work accumulates, the quota widens, so agent history becomes a crystal record that cannot be copied to a fresh account. A lantern rule keeps this visible: reputation decays when idle or when peers report bad work, so mass identities multiply the work and waiting time an attacker must pay.
